#1315. Sensational Spurs storm Stamford Bridge as Palmer loses his head

So much for Xabi Alonso’s call for cool heads from his Chelsea players. Cole Palmer lost his and was sent off, while goalkeeper Mike Penders punched the ball into his own net to give Tottenham Hotspur a helping hand on their way to a second win at Stamford Bridge in 42 attempts.

This was hardly “the Battle of the Bridge”, but Chelsea blew up during a ridiculous 10-minute spell towards the end of a game in which Tottenham had bossed possession but not looked like scoring.

Palmer was lucky to stay on the pitch in the 70th minute, when he shoved his pelvis into the face of Mateus Fernandes after the Tottenham midfielder had stopped him racing through with a foul and a handball.

Christopher Kavanagh, the referee, let him off with a yellow card, but 10 minutes later Palmer inexplicably gave Kavanagh no choice but to book him again and send him off, following a late challenge on substitute Conor Gallagher.

"It's PETULANT from Cole Palmer...you have to take it on the chin" Jamie Redknapp and Daniel Sturridge react to Cole Palmer's pair of yellow cards 🟥 https://t.co/Voxoo3Ea7V

Palmer was just about the only Chelsea player not to have been sent off last season, but it seems that Alonso has not yet managed to deal with the club’s disciplinary problem.

Jordan Henderson had given Palmer a talking to at the end of the win at Everton in which the forward was booked. But he evidently did not heed the advice or the words of his manager.

Alonso had said he was confident his players could keep calm ahead of the game, but he got that wrong – along with his team selection and substitutions.

In between Palmer’s two bookings, Penders suffered his own moment of madness with a bizarre own goal on his league debut for Chelsea. The Belgian was standing in for Emi Martinez, who watched in disbelief from the home dug-out after undergoing surgery on his jaw.

Fernandes sent in a corner that Jan Paul van Hecke challenged for. Penders looked like the easy winner in that contest, but he got his punch horribly wrong and the ball spun backwards and over the goalline.

Spurs have taken the lead after Mateus Fernandes' corner ends up in Chelsea's goal ⚽️ https://t.co/X65gyO9yPX

A man and a goal down, Chelsea then saw hundreds of their own fans walk out when Mathys Tel scored a brilliant second for Spurs with three minutes remaining. The visiting fans, who had seen one win at the Bridge since 1990 prior to Saturday, could hardly believe what they had seen.

"Just look what it means!" A glorious solo run and finish from Mathys Tel! 🤩 https://t.co/Qg7WMFNlwQ

Tottenham head coach Roberto De Zerbi celebrated wildly with his staff. The two benches had clashed and De Zerbi had been booked after Palmer’s first yellow card that the Italian felt should have been a red. But De Zerbi will not care about that now, with Tottenham’s season finally up and running thanks to successive league wins against Coventry City and Chelsea.

"They were brilliant Spurs, they really were" Gary Neville's immediate reaction to Chelsea 0-2 Tottenham 🗣️ https://t.co/QWhi7Blmfz

Tottenham should really have been ahead in the first half. De Zerbi revealed before the game that Dominic Solanke had dropped down to the substitutes’ bench because the striker “felt fatigue” after the victory over Coventry.

With Solanke resting up on the bench until the 65th minute, De Zerbi moved Omar Marmoush, who had scored his first Spurs goal against Coventry, into the middle and brought in Tel on the left.

Tel was involved in the 29th-minute move that should have resulted in the opening goal for Marmoush. The Frenchman played a one-two with Andy Robertson and the Scotsman picked out Marmoush with a low cross. But, six yards out and with time to pick his spot, the former Manchester City man allowed Penders to make a save.

The missed Marmoush chance was the first time Penders had been called into action. At the other end, Tottenham goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky made unnecessary work for himself.

Kinsky played a bad pass straight to Pedro Neto. The ball was worked to Henderson, but Kinsky recovered to make a save and then stopped the follow-up from Neto. The offside flag then went up, but it was unclear whether it would have spared Kinsky on both occasions had Chelsea scored.

It was not the first time Kinsky had handed possession back to Chelsea in a dangerous area, although the 23-year-old had also made a good save to palm away a curling effort from Palmer. That came after Fernandes had the ball pinched from him far too easily.

Neto was Chelsea’s most dangerous player, but it was the wrong call by Alonso to leave Danny Welbeck on the bench, with João Pedro out injured, and he was too slow to change things. Leaving it until the 88th minute, when the game had already been killed by Tel, to send on the striker was a clear error.

Storm Boelo created wet-and-wild conditions on the Stamford Bridge pitch, while there were still remnants of Storm Austen, or should that be Storm Austin, on the home bench.

Chelsea set-piece coach Austin MacPhee let out an incredibly loud “for f---’s sake” when one corner routine went wrong. Nobody could hear what he was shouting over the Tottenham celebrations when Penders scored his own goal, but it would almost certainly have started with “f” again.

James Maddison had been a doubt before the game after missing training during the week and it only took four minutes of the second half for him to signal to De Zerbi that he needed to come off.

Maddison had scored a brilliant goal on his first league start in 18 months against Coventry, but he had to be replaced by former Chelsea midfielder Gallagher at Stamford Bridge.

James Maddison is forced off with an injury and is replaced by Conor Gallagher, who receives a mixed reception from his former fans 🔃 https://t.co/GSeXQQ3eoa

The Chelsea fans predictably booed Gallagher, a graduate of the club’s academy who at times even stood in as captain. The foul on Gallagher that earned Palmer his marching orders silenced the jeers and the Chelsea fans’ boos only returned at the final whistle for their own players.

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso has told Cole Palmer he must learn from his red card that contributed to his team’s London derby defeat by Tottenham Hotspur.

Tottenham head coach Roberto De Zerbi insisted Palmer should have seen red for shoving his pelvis into the face of Mateus Fernandes. But, having got off with a yellow card, the Chelsea midfielder then fouled substitute Conor Gallagher.

“I haven’t seen them [the yellow cards] on TV, but as far as I have been told, he [the referee] probably got it right,” Alonso said. “So, for sure for Cole, but for everyone. We think [up until] now we haven’t received any red cards [this season] and we need to continue that way because we need to have this maturity to deal with difficult moments, when you have conceded 1-0, there was still 15-20 minutes to go, so we have to be calm. I need to check the action to talk with Cole, but it is one to learn for the future for sure.”

Asked if he thought Palmer should have been sent off for the first yellow card, De Zerbi, who was booked for his protests, replied: “Yep.”

Jordan Henderson had spoken to Palmer at the end of the previous week’s victory over Everton in which the forward could also have been booked for a second time and sent off.

But Alonso claimed he does not have any wider concerns about Palmer’s character. He said: “Today, for sure, yes, but it is not a [wider] concern. I think that Cole when he is focused on the game, when he is enjoying and today after the 1-0, it is a moment to keep calm, a moment to keep mature and for everyone.”

De Zerbi hailed his side’s character and claimed that Tottenham have “suffered enough” after two 17th-placed finishes and a slow start to the season until successive victories over Coventry City and Chelsea.

“We want to improve, improve and improve, to be better game by game, week by week. I think we have suffered enough,” De Zerbi said. “Changing the spirit of the group, changing the performance of the players, especially the more fragile players, maybe the younger players. We played very well. Great individual performances, great collective performance because we played very well. And then we put something different than Tottenham, I think, in the last period. Different attitude, different relationships with the players, different group.”

Chelsea were without João Pedro because of an injury and Alonso is waiting to find out how long the striker will be out.

“We don’t know yet because he has a lot of fluid,” Alonso said. “So he felt it yesterday [Friday] and we need to wait probably until tomorrow [Sunday] to do the test and to know the whole situation and the whole seriousness of the injury. We will know soon enough.”

A long-awaited Stamford Bridge victory for @SpursOfficial 👏 https://t.co/Qqwgbuj3Y3

“When we have dinner together and spend time together in the dressing room, I see a different group, different relationships and a different atmosphere among the players.

“The character was great today, but we have many, many new players. The players who stayed here from last season and two or three seasons ago suffered from the results, including two 17th-place finishes.

“We are working to change the last part of the club’s history. We are lucky because we have many great people in the dressing room and many great players. I think if we work hard, we can do something important.

“The week in Marbella, speaking face to face, opening ourselves up and removing the mask, was important for the spirit and belief.

“The atmosphere inside the dressing room is maybe more important than the tactics.”

Speaking to Sky Sports, the Tottenham boss said: “It was a big moment for the fans, the club and the players. They deserved this win and prepared very well.

“We are improving a lot in our mentality, as a group and in our relationships with the players. We are also improving on the pitch.

“Against Aston Villa and Everton, for 30 minutes we were playing very well. Maybe we didn’t score because our finishing wasn’t good enough, and perhaps in the first difficult moment we changed our mentality.

“Now we are a complete team. The players are playing better and we have improved our style.

“I have to believe in this group. I never lost confidence in my players.

“We have to keep working hard and improving. We have many great players, and I believe we can do something important if we continue in this way.”

"I thought our midfield was outstanding" 👏 Andy Robertson credits his Tottenham teammates after a rare win at Stamford Bridge. https://t.co/G7HpoJBZBg

"We are here to change the mentality of the club" 😤 Mateus Fernandes reacts to Spurs' win at Chelsea. https://t.co/KIGNRqDCFD

"They were brilliant Spurs, they really were" Gary Neville's immediate reaction to Chelsea 0-2 Tottenham 🗣️ https://t.co/QWhi7Blmfz

Tottenham have a rare and fully deserved victory over 10-man Chelsea at Stamford Bridge. An own goal from Penders and Tel’s brilliant solo strike sealed the three points for De Zerbi’s side. Chelsea produced a dreadful performance with Palmer sent off in the second half to compound a miserable evening for the hosts.

Three GLORIOUS points at Stamford Bridge 🤩 https://t.co/czWx6bUB78

Chelsea supporters have emptied Stamford Bridge. Tottenham fans are making all the noise. The visitors have been better in every department on the pitch today.

Rogers is booked for an ugly challenge on Gallagher. Amid the chaos, Welbeck finally enters the action, replacing Pedro Neto, while Kulusevski and Davies come on for Tel and Kudus. There’s seven minutes of added time.

Spurs are on their way to a historic win at Stamford Bridge. Tel starts a dribble from inside his own half, escapes Acheampong and glides past Lacroix, before arrowing a clinical effort into the bottom corner, sending De Zerbi and the away support absolutely wild. Incredible scenes. Chelsea have been miles off the pace today.

"Just look what it means!" A glorious solo run and finish from Mathys Tel! 🤩 https://t.co/Qg7WMFNlwQ

Kudus wins the ball off Palestra and tees up Gallagher, who shoots from a tight angle, but his low drive is parried away by Penders.

It goes from bad to worse for Chelsea. Palmer catches Gallagher with a late tackle and stamps on his ankle. It’s a definite second yellow card, and despite the Chelsea protests, Palmer can have no complaints. Chelsea have a mountain to climb now with a numerical disadvantage.

Cole Palmer is SENT OFF! 🟥 https://t.co/qArrUhFrf0

Penders comes out to claim a corner and mistimes his punch, directing the ball into the Chelsea net for an own goal, despite Lacroix’s best efforts to keep it from crossing the line. It’s a calamitous error from Penders on his first Premier League start. Tottenham have a priceless goal at Stamford Bridge and they deserve it.

Spurs have taken the lead after Mateus Fernandes' corner ends up in Chelsea's goal ⚽️ https://t.co/X65gyO9yPX

Estevao is on for Chelsea and replaces Quenda. The Brazilian is involved straight away as he strides into the penalty area and shoots into the side netting.

There’s a scuffle between both sets of players. Van de Ven lunges in with a late challenge on Caicedo, before Mateus Fernandes slips over and handles the ball as Palmer attempts to dribble forward. The Englishman reacts angrily, barging into Fernandes to spark a mini scuffle. Palmer is booked for that flashpoint. It was a foolish and risky challenge from the Chelsea man.

Things are heating up at the Bridge as Cole Palmer and Mateus Fernandes both receive a yellow! 🟨 https://t.co/hYXFl6xlZi

Here comes a Chelsea change, but it’s not an attacking one. It arrives at full back, with Palestra replacing Hato.

De Zerbi then makes a double substitution as Solanke and Porro come on for Marmoush and Robertson.

Can any of these alterations inject some more life into this encounter?

Neto forces a save from Kinsky. Chelsea pounce on Mateus Fernandes’ wayward pass, allowing Palmer and Neto to combine. The latter fizzes a venomous effort straight at Kinsky, which he bats away. That’s Chelsea’s best chance for some time.

How long will Alonso wait before introducing some substitutes for Chelsea? The hosts’ attacking threat is notably lacking. Welbeck and Estevao must be itching to enter the action.

This game is still being played at a relatively slow pace and is lacking some serious bite. Will Maddison’s injury take the wind out of Spurs’ sails or inspire them to victory?

Confirmation of that change as Gallagher replaces the injured Maddison, who heads straight down the tunnel. There’s some boos for Gallagher on his return to his former employers.

James Maddison is forced off with an injury and is replaced by Conor Gallagher, who receives a mixed reception from his former fans 🔃 https://t.co/GSeXQQ3eoa

There’s a break in play as Maddison goes down without anyone around him and glumly sits on the floor. He just can’t stay fit. Former Chelsea captain Gallagher is getting ready to come on.

Palmer surges forward before tumbling to the floor, believing he was clipped by Mateus Fernandes. There’s half-hearted appeals from some Chelsea players for a free kick on the edge of Spurs’ penalty area, but the referee isn’t interested.

We are back under way for the second half. Both sides are unchanged at the break. Will we be treated to a more exiting second half? Let’s hope so.

It’s half-time at Stamford Bridge in a game lacking chances and attacking threat. Tottenham came closest to scoring just before the half-hour mark, when Marmoush forced Penders into terrific save on his first Premier League start. At the other end, Palmers tested Kinsky with a whipped effort, which the Spurs goalkeeper parried away. There’s much to ponder for Chelsea boss Alonso, whose plan to start to without a recognised striker has underwhelmed, while De Zerbi will feel more encouraged by his side’s display.

Hato takes a quick, clever free kick and finds Pedro Neto, whose made a great run. The winger flashes a low, driven shot off the wet surface from a tight angle, but Kinsky is there to gather it.

Spurs come forward on the counter through Tel, Marmoush and Kudus. However, the attack seems to lack conviction and it ends with Mateus Fernandes’ arrowed cross harmlessly drifting out of play.

We’re still waiting for this game to explode into life. It’s lacked the normal drama and controversy that this fixture normally provides.

Chelsea come alive as Kinsky miscues his pass, giving the ball to Pedro Neto. Palmer and Rogers get involved in the attack and it ends with a placed Henderson shot, which Kinsky does well to parry away. Chelsea look most dangerous when Kinsky has the ball at his feet and gives it away. The Tottenham goalkeeper needs to be careful.

Spurs burst forward on the counter and threads a pass through to Tel. Penders rushes out to smother the winger’s one-on-one effort. The offside flag was up, but Penders still did well to make the intervention.

Massive chance for Tottenham. Robertson slides a low, pinpoint cross into Marmoush, who shoots first-time from close range. Penders is up to the challenge and makes a pivotal stop to parry it away.

Penders comes out of his box and unconvincingly intercepts a through ball over the top of Chelsea’s defence. His pass has no power, but luckily for the young goalkeeper, it lands at Lacroix’s feet.

Spurs aren’t playing with their usual inferiority complex at Stamford Bridge. They looking confident. Chelsea are yet to strike a rhythm. Tel darts into Chelsea’s box, but Pedro Neto tracks back and makes an important tackle.

Chelsea’s substitutes have just been handed fluffy white towels to keep themselves dry and warm. I want one.

Tel’s deep cross finds Kudus at the back stick. The Ghanaian bends a curling strike around the covering defender. However, the shot evades the far post. Tottenham can certainly be encouraged by their start to this game.

Lacroix denies Maddison with a brilliant sliding challenge to win a goal kick for Chelsea. Maddison was convinced it was a corner.

We just heard a rather loud “For f***s sake” from Chelsea set-piece coach Austin MacPhee. Given we’ve just had Storm Austen, it feels appropriate that the Scotsman is giving the players a battering.

Pedro Neto does excellently to dispossess Mateus Fernandes, allowing Rogers to tee up Palmer. The playmaker whips a fierce effort aimed for the far top corner, but Kinsky is there to make a eye-catching diving save.

Tottenham have had more of the early possession, but both teams are still sounding each other out as we await the game’s first big chance. Palmers, Rogers and Henderson attempt a cheeky free kick routine, but Kinsky is alert to the danger.

Kinsky comes out of his box and Chelsea pounce on his poor pass to launch an attack. Palmer fizzes a delightful cross into the box, but no one is there to get on the end of it. Where’s Joao Pedro when you need him?

Rogers is playing highest for Chelsea as a false striker. He did it a few times for Villa, so it shouldn’t be anything new to him.

An early spell of Tottenham sees Chelsea defend a couple of free-kicks and clear a corner.

There will be no out-and-out strikers on the pitch today. Joao Pedro is out for Chelsea with an, as yet unspecified injury, while De Zerbi has said that Dominic Solanke “felt fatigue” against Coventry City so he has dropped to the bench. Antonio Conte, a former manager of both of these teams, wouldn’t be having a player missing a London derby for “feeling fatigue”.

Chelsea get us under way. The rain is hammering down on the pitch.

Can Spurs get their second win at Stamford Bridge, or will Chelsea's dominance continue? 👀📊 https://t.co/dNYgN2SKYA

These two bitter rivals meet again. The noise inside Stamford Bridge is deafening.

Cesar Azpilicueta is back at Stamford Bridge today. The club’s former captain relished a London derby and, more often than not, finished on the winning side against Spurs. Predictably he was given a big cheer by the home fans and loudly booed by the away end.

Roberto De Zerbi has made two changes to the side that beat Coventry. Dominic Solanke and Tosin Adarabioyo are replaced by Mathys Tel and Mateus Fernandes. After scoring on Monday night, James Maddison retains his starting position in the line-up, while Dejan Kulusevski continues on the bench.

Our Tottenham side to face Chelsea ✊ 🔢 @krakenfx https://t.co/GggamSkkLY

Our Chelsea. 💙 #CFC | #CHETOT https://t.co/G5ua5Ufr3Y

Chelsea goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez has been ruled for a “few weeks” after he collided with Jarrad Branthwaite and undergoing surgery on his jaw.

Speaking on the issue, Xabi Alonso said: “Emi is doing better. He had the surgery and day by day he is feeling better, but we still need to wait. A few weeks. Hopefully, less than more, but we need to wait.

“The good thing is that he is feeling better and we need to listen to his feelings, the opinions of the doctors, the specialists, the surgeons. Considering it was a bad one, he is doing good.”

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this mouthwatering Premier League game between Chelsea and Tottenham at Stamford Bridge.

Chelsea secured a hard-fought 2-0 away win at Everton last weekend thanks to Pedro Neto’s double, while Tottenham earned their first Premier League victory of the season on Monday, beating Frank Lampard’s Coventry City 3-1 at home.

It’s Xabi Alonso’s first taste of the bitter rivalry and has hyped up the atmosphere ahead of the clash. “We are expecting a good atmosphere,” he said. “Electric, with good energy, knowing that in a derby this passion is really in the air in the stadium.

“We need that connection with the crowd in good moments. There will be tough moments, but we need to pull together and play our game. For me, it’s fundamental that we play our game on the pitch.

“The players, they do their best, but when the crowd is playing the game, is living it, that’s the good thing about the Premier League. I think the crowd plays the game as well. It’s not that they just watch the game.”

Chelsea will be without Emiliano Martinez, who fractured his jaw against Everton, with Mike Penders poised to start. Reece James, Pep Chavarria and Emmanuel Emegha are also ruled out.

As for Tottenham, Rodrigo Bentancur remains suspended, while Destiny Udogie, Lucas Bergvall, Wilson Odobert and Xavi Simons are unavailable. James Maddison and Dejan Kulusevski enjoyed happy returns to the first team against Coventry following lengthy injuries and could feature here.

It’s safe to say that the statistics aren’t on Spurs’ side. Roberto De Zerbi will be well aware of Tottenham’s dismal record at Stamford Bridge, where Spurs have won just once in 41 across all competitions. Tottenham have also only beaten once in their 15 previous Premier League meetings – a 2-0 victory over Graham Potter’s Chelsea in 2023.

Games between these bitter rivals always carry a feistiness and an added edge. Drama is guaranteed. Kick-off is at 17:30, with team news coming shortly.

#1314. Mauricio Pochettino is CONFIRMED as new Man United manager: Departing USA boss speaks out as he agrees to succeed Michael Carrick - but faces race against time for first game

Published: 07:02 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 07:51 EST, 13 November 2026

Manchester United have confirmed that Mauricio Pochettino has agreed to become their new head coach on a two-and-a-half-year contract at Old Trafford.

Pochettino will replace Michael Carrick who was sacked following 10 months in charge on Friday, after United agreed to pay more than £10million to buy him and his backroom staff out of their contracts with the US Soccer Federation.

The 54-year-old Argentine will take charge of the USA’s CONCACAF Nations League double-header against Haiti in Miami on Saturday and Cincinnati on Wednesday before beginning his new job as United boss on Wednesday. His first game will be against Liverpool at Anfield a week on Sunday.

There were no comments from Pochettino or United officials in Friday’s press release confirming his appointment because he remains contracted to US Soccer.

Pochettino said in the USMNT's statement: 'The opportunity to represent the USA crest was one of the greatest honors of my career. We are so grateful to the players for their commitment, to the fans for their belief, and to the Federation for always supporting our staff and creating the opportunities to impact the culture of soccer in this great country.'

Pochettino is due to give a pre-match press conference at 2.15pm on Friday, but is not expected to speak about United until he arrives next week.

United sources say that Pochettino’s experience, philosophy, personality and skill-set make him well suited for the job, as well as his record of developing individual talent and building excellent team cultures.

Mauricio Pochettino has been appointed as the Manchester United manager

Michael Carrick was sacked after the club made their worst start to the season in 40 years

A statement from the club read: ‘Mauricio Pochettino has agreed to become the Manchester United men’s head coach from 18 November.

‘The club has reached an agreement with the US Soccer Federation for Mauricio and his staff to be released after the conclusion of their responsibilities with the US men’s national team.

‘The Argentinian is renowned for his high-intensity, attacking style of football, his dedication to building strong, cohesive teams and his outstanding record of developing individual players.

‘Pochettino has consistently performed at the highest level of football across multiple leagues. He began his coaching career with Espanyol in 2009 before joining Southampton and achieving a club-record Premier League points tally in 2014.

‘During five full seasons at Tottenham Hotspur, Pochettino established the club as regular UEFA Champions League contenders, securing qualification in four consecutive seasons and leading the club to its first final in the competition in 2019.

‘In 2021, he joined Paris Saint-Germain, where he won the Ligue 1 title, the Coupe de France and the Trophée des Champions before joining Chelsea in 2023. Most recently he led the U.S. Men’s National Team to the Round of 16 at the FIFA World Cup.’

Earlier in the week, the club's chief executive Omar Berrada and Wilcox flew back from Monaco, where minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe ratified their decision to sack Carrick with the blessing of co-chairmen Joel and Avram Glazer.

Carrick arrived at United's training ground at 7.50am on Thursday morning and was dismissed.

He left at 10.18am, less than two and a half hours later. He became the first Premier League manager to be sacked this season.

United's statement read: 'After a disappointing start to the season, the club has come to the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions.

'Michael is, and always will be, a Manchester United legend. Just as he did as a player, he has conducted himself with the highest standards of dedication and professionalism throughout his time back with the club.

'His leadership and achievements last season will always be fondly remembered.'

Sources close to United say the club's leadership believe their squad of players is far better than the performances and results under Carrick indicated.

United feel that the squad are far better than their position in the Premier League shows

They gave the under-fire manager a chance to turn things around against Chelsea, Roma and Aston Villa but ultimately felt the team were not on the right path.

It has been a campaign in which United won just three matches, one of which came against Azerbaijani minnows FK Sabah, and they are yet to keep a clean sheet in the league.

Pochettino's United travel to Anfield on November 22 before a Champions League clash at Sporting Lisbon, Pochettino's first home game against Brentford and then away match at Newcastle.

#1312. Serie A CEO De Siervo elected new chair of the World Leagues Association

Lega Serie A CEO Luigi De Siervo has been elected as the new Chair of the World Leagues Association for four years, taking over from Premier League CEO Richard Masters.

The group has been going for 10 years and brought together over 100 representatives of football leagues around the world for the annual meeting in Czechia today.

In a boost for the role of Italian football on the global stage, Serie A chief De Siervo was elected the new Chair of the World Leagues Association.

He will have a four-year mandate, and succeed Premier League figurehead Masters, whose term had come to its natural conclusion.

Masters will remain as Vice-Chair of the WLA alongside Don Garber, the Commissioner of Major League Soccer in the USA.

“I am honoured to have been elected Chair of the World Leagues Association at such an important moment,” said De Siervo.

“Over the past ten years, the WLA has steadily grown, bringing together 51 leagues from across all continents. It reflects the importance of cooperation and of giving national leagues a stronger voice in the governance of world football.”

De Siervo has been the CEO of the Lega Serie A since December 2018, during a particularly difficult period for Italian football.

The World Leagues Association was founded in 2016 and represents 51 professional leagues across the globe, hoping to strengthen the role of nations leagues in football governance.

Published: 09:58 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 11:57 EST, 13 November 2026

Usman Nurmagomedov and his entourage have been swiftly punished with prison sentences and fines in Abu Dhabi after their shocking hotel attack.

Nurmagomedov set upon UFC star Merab Dvalishvili on Wednesday, slapping him in the lobby of Yas Hilton hotel in a revenge mission filmed by his friends.

The Georgian-American Dvalishvili then retaliated and fought back with his cameraman as the melee rapidly descended into complete mayhem. Dvalishvili was left bloodied and bruised and the attackers were quickly detained by the authorities.

Six of the attackers were given six-month prison sentences and ordered to pay £61,000 each in fines. They will also be immediately deported  when their sentences end.

Nurmagomedov and his team's violent ambush was four months in the making.

UFC star Merab Dvalishvili was attacked in a five-star hotel in Abu Dhabi on Wednesday

'It’s between me and Umar… I have so much respect for all Dagestani people, especially fighters. The only guy who I don't like from Dagestan is Umar and his sneaky manager, Rizvan. The guy who was helping Umar disrespect me on X and Threads.'

After Gadzhimagomedov squared up to him, Dvalishvili shoved him in the neck, shouting: 'What's your problem, b***h!'

The situation, unlike the hotel brawl that escalated into a complete bloodbath, was quickly defused and there was a child in close proximity.

Usman wanted to take revenge on behalf of fellow Dagestani Gadzhimagomedov and also his brother Umar, who lost against Dvalishvili in a title shot last year.

In the footage of the hotel attack, the group appeared to approach Dvalishvili, 35, from behind, before one man said a couple of words to him and slapped him in the face.

Dvalishvili was rocked, then kicked, and was held back by a man he appeared to be with.

He tried to fight back but a number of men overwhelmed him as his companion was attacked too. Eventually, the groups were separated, and Dvalishvili took to social media to respond to the incident.

Just two of us, me and my friend, came here in Abu Dhabi and Usman and his friends came like snakes from behind. What kind of fighters are you guys? What kind of man does this? His companion then added: 'From behind? You call yourselves men? You're a little b***h.'

Dvalishvili continued: 'You are sneaky guys. You are not real men. It shows your guys' character, what the f*** guys? If you want to fight, let's fight. We are fighters. I talk straight, but you guys came from behind. I don't know how many guys, all your friends waiting for us in a sneaky way, wow.

'I knew guys, I knew what kind of guys you were. Usman, Umar and his friends came sneaky from behind, so many guys. Wow. I am fine guys. All my friends and family, I am f***ing fine. I am a fighter. #1310. Engineered bacteria are weaning farms away from synthetic fertilizers

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Mariana Lenharo is a reporter for Nature in New York City.

Scientists are engineering bacteria that can provide nitrogen, an essential ingredient for plant growth, to wheat crops. Credit: Shakeel Ahmed/Anadolu Agency/Getty

The world’s farms depend on synthetic nitrogen fertilizers to increase crop yields, but the production and use of these chemicals generates billions of tonnes of greenhouse-gas emissions every year. Now, scientists are making progress on a greener alternative: bioengineered bacteria.

This approach takes a cue from natural bacteria that ‘fix’ nitrogen into a useful form and provide it to certain plants. Scientists are engineering genetic features into bacteria with the aim of enabling them to fix nitrogen for important food crops, such as maize (corn) and wheat, that don’t have such natural microbial partners.

In a comment published on 10 November in Nature Biotechnology1, researchers suggest that bioengineered bacteria could eventually replace up to half of synthetic fertilizers. The bacteria deliver nitrogen more efficiently to roots than synthetic fertilizers do, which could reduce greenhouse-gas emissions and nitrogen pollution of waterways. But this would require a slew of advances, from getting different microbial species to work together to more-rigorous field trials.

How CRISPR could yield the next blockbuster cropSome of these ‘biofertilizers’ have been augmented with genes and genetic snippets from viruses or distantly related bacteria. This means that the engineered microbes are classified as transgenic — altered to include DNA from other species. The bacteria are now being trialled on small plots of maize on farms in the Midwestern United States. The bacteria, developed by Switch Bioworks in San Carlos, California, are the first example of a transgenic biofertilizer approved for testing on fields in the country.

How CRISPR could yield the next blockbuster crop

In September, Switch Bioworks received approval from the Brazilian regulatory agency, the National Technical Commission on Biosafety (CNTBio), to test its strains there. This is the first time that a transgenic bacterium of any kind has been approved for field tests in Brazil, says molecular biologist Mario Murakami, who is the president of CTNBio in Campinas.

Companies that have focused on editing bacterial genes rather than producing transgenic microbes are further along. Pivot Bio in Minneapolis, Minnesota, has applied its gene-edited biofertilizers to tens of millions of hectares of US farmland over the past decade, says the company’s chief technology officer Travis Frey. Some of Pivot Bio’s products have also been tested in Canada, Argentina, Kenya and Brazil.

Most plants can’t use the form of nitrogen that is present in the air. Some crops, including soya beans and peanuts, host colonies of bacteria that can convert atmospheric nitrogen into a usable form. The plant takes up that nitrogen and, in return, provides carbon that fuels bacterial growth. But most staple crops lack these microbial partners, leading farmers to rely on synthetic nitrogen fertilizers. These chemical fertilizers account for 5% of global greenhouse-gas emissions, and drive damaging nutrient pollution in waterways.

For decades, researchers have tried to get bacteria to fix nitrogen for staple crops. Until recently, the approach was to collect wild strains of nitrogen-fixing bacteria from soil and apply them to seeds or spray them onto plants. “It doesn’t work,” says Jean-Michel Ané, a bioengineer at the University of Wisconsin–Madison, who is working on microbial fertilizers. The wild microbes fail to thrive when applied to crops that don’t provide them with carbon.

How to climate-proof crops: scientists say the secret’s in the dirt

How to climate-proof crops: scientists say the secret’s in the dirt

#1308. Most expensive goal in Liverpool history gives Iraola era lift-off

A quick sprint, a well-placed pass and an instinctive finish. Bradley Barcola and Alexander Isak will have done this dozens of times in training but here, on a squally Sunday afternoon, this combination secured a little piece of history.

Anfield has witnessed plenty of significant goals down the years but never had this crowd seen one that cost £248m to make. Liverpool invested a near quarter-billion pounds on Barcola and Isak for bigger occasions than a tussle with Brighton and Hove Albion, but this rapid interchange felt like a significant moment.

Liverpool are a work in progress under Andoni Iraola but with each minute of each game you can see signs of things knitting together, and if Barcola and Isak are finding harmony, with Florian Wirtz in behind, then, perhaps, this journey will start to accelerate.

This was an important afternoon for Liverpool’s head coach, a difficult assignment against high-flying, well-respected opponents in Brighton, who arrived on Merseyside having won their last four Premier League fixtures with a combined aggregate of 15-0, including a 3-0 thumping of reigning champions Arsenal.

But Liverpool rose impressively to the challenge and there are grounds for saying this was the most significant success to date for Iraola, whose team defended relentlessly to preserve a clean sheet. They are up to fourth now after this 2-0 success and deserve their position.

“I’m very happy,” Iraola said. “We faced a very good opponent, similar to Villarreal [in the Champions League]. It’s difficult to defend them a lot of times and it was key how we started. We needed to be aggressive, recover balls, win our duels, be dangerous in transitions: I think we’ve done it.”

And how. Iraola was able to march towards the Kop at the end, to clap the supporters and acknowledge only Liverpool’s fifth (and his first) Premier League win at Anfield in 2026, and it was evident he had a spring in his step from what he had seen.

Whether the game would have flowed in the direction it did had Brighton taken the lead can only be speculated but what a glorious chance they wasted for us to find out: in the 13th minute, five swift, one-touch passes bamboozled Liverpool’s defence and created space for Yasin Ayari.

With the goal at his mercy, Ayari could have made things exceptionally uncomfortable but he leant back and blazed over. He clasped his face and grimaced, knowing what had gone begging in front of the Kop; four minutes later, his misery was exacerbated.

"He's GOT to hit the target!" Yasin Ayari missed a golden chance to put Brighton ahead against Liverpool 🫣 https://t.co/Qz7G3sXCpP

Liverpool’s lead was secured with an element of good fortune but, equally, the tenacity of Ronald Araújo and Wirtz was instrumental in pressing Brighton back to the point that they were panicking; Wirtz’s shot, deflected off Pascal Gross past Bart Verbruggen, compounded it all.

“I think everyone in the stadium – and you as well – felt there was a missed opportunity for us,” groaned Fabian Hürzeler, the visitors’ head coach. “It’s not only after the goal or the goals they scored. Before they scored, we had two big chances. I think it was just the difference that they scored and we didn’t score.”

It would be wrong to say Wirtz was doing cartwheels – perhaps he knew immediately he would not get the goal – but it was an important moment for him and you could feel the sense of goodwill towards him from team-mates and supporters alike.

Florian Wirtz's deflected shot has put Liverpool ahead minutes after Brighton had a great chance of their own ⚽️ https://t.co/b6mRvl2rSR

Remarkably, this was the first time Liverpool had scored in the first half at Anfield in a Premier League fixture since May 9 and, with that momentum, it led to one of those periods when they started attacking in waves and carried the crowd with them.

What they needed was a second goal to arrive quite quickly and that is what happened when Barcola won possession, scuttled forward and played a perfectly weighted bobbling ball into Isak’s path; the Swede did the rest, calmly finishing from eight yards.

Everything with Isak feels to be going under the radar at the moment, but that is six goals in six Premier League appearances. He is starting to show the consistency and killer instinct that everyone felt he would. Iraola will be hoping it continues for the foreseeable future.

Alexander Isak scores to double Liverpool's lead at Anfield! 💥 https://t.co/oYs2jnHZEb

“The performance was really good,” said Isak, the quiet assassin. “We were really solid against a really good team. The first half is what we really want to be about. It was about intensity, winning balls and countering.”

Brighton, as much as Hürzeler protested, could not properly recover, though this is no criticism. They remain committed to attack, they struck the frame of the goal when Ayari tried to punish an Alisson Becker mistake and the desire to keep pushing ensured Liverpool could never relax.

What Liverpool had going for them this time, however, was an intensity to preserve a clean sheet and nobody embodied the indefatigability more than Araújo, the Uruguay international whose loan from Barcelona is looking an increasingly shrewd piece of business.

Two moments stood out: one thunderous tackle on substitute Malick Yalcouyé in front of the Main Stand that had the locals roaring their approval, another in the first half when he was on the floor but still managed to head away to thwart Maxim De Cuyper.

They remember those moments as much as the stardust that Barcola and Isak provide. Put it all together and it might just be a launchpad for Iraola.

"The performance was really solid" Alexander Isak reacts after scoring in Liverpool's win against Brighton 🗣️ https://t.co/Zei2tmWVix

Iraola has his first Premier League home win in charge of Liverpool thanks to a 2-0 victory over Brighton. The hosts netted twice in the first half through Wirtz’s deflected strike off Gross and Isak’s close-range finish. This result moves Liverpool above Chelsea and up to fourth, just a point behind third-place Brighton, who suffer their first defeat in any competition since August 30.

Three points at Anfield 😍 #LIVBHA https://t.co/AnAlNgOzlu

Still, Brighton can’t find a way through Liverpool’s resilient defence. Araujo’s well-time sliding challenge on Kostoulas draws huge cheers from the home fans.

Ronald Araujo has become a cult figure very quickly and he’s just provided the moment of the second half with a challenge that was a well received by those in the Main Stand as a goal. Liverpool are working relentlessly to preserve their clean sheet and Andoni Iraola is imploring his players to retain their focus until the end.

There will be four minutes of added time. Brighton need a goal as soon as possible. Liverpool are closing in on an impressive win.

So wasteful from Brighton... They have a great chance to put the ball into the box with a free kick, but De Cuyper wastefully launches it out of play. With Gross also stood over it, you expected him take it. Liverpool then make a late change as Tsimikas replaces Kerkez for the final few minutes.

Gakpo drives forward and smashes a wild long-range shot wide. His end-product has been lacking today, but he’s undoubtedly caused Brighton problems with his dribbling, movement and directness.

A spell of Brighton pressure ends as Rutter can’t quite find Kostoulas with a low cross. The young striker stays down and replays show that Jacquet stood on his foot as the defender attempted a clearance. However, it’s quickly checked and cleared by VAR. There wasn’t much in the challenge at all.

Kerkez scampers into Brighton’s box, reaching the byline, but he can’t dig out a cross as the chance disappears. Brighton will need to throw everything forward soon.

Now, that double change from Liverpool is here. Barcola and Isak depart to large applause, with Ngumoha and Koumas cheered on as they run onto the pitch.

As expected, Rutter is on. He replaces Ayari, who will think back to his missed chance and shot off the post in the first half.

Gakpo brilliantly turns Costinha, who pulls the winger back to deservedly pick up a booking. Both sides look to be readying changes, with Ngumoha, Koumas and Rutter poised to enter the action.

Brighton seem to have hit a wall in this second half. They’ve struggled to create chances since the break. Liverpool are working really hard defensively.

Once again, Liverpool break through Gakpo. This time, it comes from a Brighton corner, but Gakpo’s cross for Isak at the back post is read by Dunk.

In his first involvement since entering the action, Nyoni ends a slick Brighton move by taking the ball off De Cuyper’s toe in the penalty area with a much-needed clearance. He seems to be limping after he was caught by De Cuyper.

Wirtz’s game is over and he departs to be replaced by Nyoni in Liverpool’s first change.

After some treatment for Wirtz, Vuskovic eventually takes the free kick. It’s in such an inviting position, but the defender gets too power on his strike and whips it over the bar.

This game is still very much in the balance, even though Liverpool have a two goal advantage, and it speaks volumes about both teams’ commitment to attack. The questions the respective head coaches are asking of their players are relentless but the players are responding by being adventurous in how they attack and where they want to get on the ball. How Andoni Iraola and Fabian Hurzeler deploy their substitutes will be significant.

Liverpool are holding firm, with Brighton yet to create an opportunity in this second half. Ayari is apprehended by Wirtz to win a free kick on the edge of the area. Despite committing the foul, Wirtz has stayed down and is clutching his ankle.

Brighton make another change and it’s a straight swap in midfield as Yalcouye replaces Chema Andres, who hobbles off the pitch.

With Brighton requiring at least two goals to avoid defeat, they’ll need to push a lot of men forward, which will open up space for Liverpool to exploit on the break. If there is one, the next goal in this game is crucial.

Liverpool break through Gakpo, who sprints from inside his own half into the penalty. He tries to release Isak, but his pass is intercepted by Vuskovic as he’s swarmed by the Brighton defence. Gakpo waited too long and should have played the pass earlier.

Kerkez isn’t switched on and fails to deal with a long ball, allowing Gomez to race in behind. Van Dijk covers Kerkez and blocks Gomez’s pass, with Kostoulas sprinting up in support.

We are back under way for the second half. Hurzeler has made one half-time alteration, with Hinshelwood replacing Boscagli, who was booked just before the break. Meanwhile, Liverpool are unchanged as they look to protect their two-goal advantage.

Wirtz’s wickedly deflected strike off Gross and Isak’s neat finish from close range mean Liverpool are two goals in front against Brighton. The visitors have also looked dangerous going forward, with Ayari wasting a golden chance when the score was still goalless, before hitting the post in the 36th minute. As it stands, this result would move Liverpool into fourth and a point behind Brighton, who need a massive second-half performance.

Two goals to the good for @LFC 😮‍💨 A Pascal Gross own goal puts the Reds ahead, before Alexander Isak fires in the second 🔴 https://t.co/AglQOyUIoY

Brighton are desperate to find a goal before the break as Kostoulas’ fierce shot is batted away by Alisson, whose goal is living a charmed life. Boscagli then receives a yellow card for blocking Barcola’s off-the-ball run.

No getting away from the fact that Brighton simply haven’t got started and it’s a huge surprise. What chances they have had came from Liverpool’s own shortcomings and it is impossible to think they will be so off the pace in the second period. Fabian Hurzeler has remained composed, which is more than can be said for Oliver Boscagli, who looks like he is playing pass the parcel, so anxious is he to get rid of the ball - often with a mistake.

On the counter, Gomez tries to find Ayari with a pass, but Jacquet’s touch knocks the ball out of Liverpool’s box. There will be three minutes of added time to end this half.

Araujo forces a save as he sprints forward from his right-back position to receive a clipped pass from Mac Allister, before shooting from a tight angle to sting the palms of Verbruggen with a drilled effort.

Gakpo drives at Brighton’s defence and then nearly squeezes a low cross to the supporting Isak, but Dunk’s crucial intervention with his outstretched leg prevents a chance.

Off the post for Brighton. Ayari shoots from an incredibly long way out as Brighton dispossess Mac Allister and Jacquet, however his curling effort agonisingly bounces against the post and out, with Alisson well beaten.

Despite falling two goals behind in this first half, Brighton have recorded 83% possession over the previous five minutes.

There’s a small confrontation between Vuskovic and Gakpo, which is quickly checked and cleared by VAR. In the next passage of play, Kerkez tees up Gakpo, who bursts into the box and reaches the byline, but his cross is blocked by Dunk.

A smooth Brighton move ends with Jacquet making a crucial block to deny Kostoulas from close range. Liverpool eventually scramble it clear. That’s a reminder of the threat that Brighton can pose.

Brighton look stunned. Since Ayari missed that chance, they’ve been swarmed by Liverpool, whose forwards are in the mood for some goals today.

Two goals in quick succession propel Liverpool into a commanding lead. So much credit must go to Barcola. He closes down Boscagli, beats the defender to the loose ball with his blistering pace and then delivers a pinpoint cross towards Isak, who gets across his marker at the near post to direct a first-time finish into the far bottom corner.

#1307. Former Old Firm rivals reveal how clubs walked a fine line between rivalry and respect...and even stopped by for tea and sympathy in times of trouble!

Published: 12:20 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 12:29 EST, 13 November 2026

They have reached an age when they would once have been categorised as the old infirm. Yet in the autumn of 2026 they cavort around Toryglen with an almost juvenile vigour.

They have reached the age when they can reflect on being stalwarts of the Old Firm. Yet they are outlining plans and strategy for a vital, growing movement.

The two meetings are separated by two sets of stairs. On the ground level, men of pensionable age and beyond play walking football. Just above sit Campbell Ogilvie, former secretary of Rangers and president of the Scottish FA, and Eric Riley, once company secretary and director of Celtic.

They are both on the board of Walking Football Scotland, an organisation that now has more than 5,000 people playing the game across 160 clubs, with participants ranging from 40 to 93.

The venerable statesmen of the Scottish game may be perceived to be rivals, but only in matters on the pitch. They sit in an office in the south side of Glasgow and reminisce about how they first met 50 years ago when playing five-a-sides and then renewed that rivalry in their professional life.

As the Glasgow rivals now seem regularly at odds, both men recalled a time when friendship was paramount amid the sporting mayhem.

Former Rangers secretary Campbell Ogilvie and ex-Celtic director Eric Riley are firm friends

‘The two clubs always had a good relationship back in those days,’ said Ogilvie, now 76 and still playing football. ‘We wanted to beat each other — naturally. But off the field we had a very close relationship.’

He told a remarkable story that backs that assertion.

‘There was one day I was at Ibrox in the early 1980s when the team was not doing so well. The phone rang and it was Sean Fallon, Jock Stein’s former Celtic assistant. I had known Sean from my days with the Scottish League and he said: “I know you’re going through a rocky spell, so I’m coming over for a cup of tea”.

‘Over he comes. So there was a very close relationship in those days. I’m not there now and for all I know there still is. But certainly, when I was there and Eric was at Celtic, we could talk to each other.’

Riley, 69, agreed: ‘Absolutely. John McClelland (former Rangers chairman) was one we could talk to. And Martin (Bain, former chief executive) I suppose, when he came along a bit later. Between myself and Peter Lawwell (former Celtic chief executive and chairman) the relationship between the clubs off the field was actually quite strong. But on the field we still wanted to win.’

Ogilvie added: ‘There was a respect. And I go back to the Willie Waddells and the Willie Thorntons, there was that respect. More recently that was there with the likes of Jack McGinn and so on.

‘We had a good relationship but it’s fair to say that there was no social media in those days. You know all the toxic stuff that can bring.’

The traits of respect and sporting competitiveness have been obvious in both men since they first met half a century ago. ‘We played five-a-side football at Scotstoun before the football careers started. It was just casual games,’ said Ogilvie. ‘We were in our early 20s. Eric was an accountant and I think those games were arranged through accountants.

‘I played youth football when I was 16 and, 60 years down the line, playing football is still a major part of my life.’

Ogilvie began walking football eight years ago and Riley soon after. ‘I suffer from Parkinson’s, amongst other things,’ said Riley. ‘I was getting assistance through Stobhill Hospital and the physiotherapist there, who specialises in Parkinson’s patients, got in touch to say there was a project going on at Toryglen where they were playing walking football and assessing you to see what the benefits may or may not be.’

Ogilvie and Riley are both on the board of Walking Football and have played a big role in its rise

Riley agreed to take part. ‘I really enjoyed it because you are back playing football again, you have the camaraderie and you have the home baking which I never really get at home.’

Riley had a hip replacement in March and admitted: ‘I have not played since then. I miss it. I play a few other things which are more and more difficult. I play tennis.’

His tennis history is illustrious as he played with Judy Murray in Scottish championships. ‘She went off to the tour and I went off to university,’ says Riley. He is unstinting in his praise of the woman who became the mother of the No1 in men’s singles and men’s doubles.

The repartee between Riley and Ogilvie is relaxed but both men have a resolve to grow walking football. Their task has been helped by bookmakers William Hill stepping in with sponsorship.

The benefits of the sport stretch beyond the physical. Ogilvie gave his own experience.

‘When you have finished working, there is a void, not mixing with people, not being with people, and walking football certainly has helped me fill that. Hopefully it helps me keep a bit fitter too,’ he said.

Ogilvie pointed out: ‘The issues you tend to encounter are health. Grief is another one. There are quite a few of the guys who have lost their wives and quite a few who are just sitting on the sofa watching Homes Under the Hammer.’

Walking football, too, has attracted a large cadre of women. ‘One of the things that stood out for me was the number of females playing,’ said Riley. ‘I went along to my first session and there were four female players, three of whom had never kicked a football in their life previously. Walking football got them involved and they really enjoyed it.’

Walking football has made giant leaps in Scotland but the next step is to collate data so cases for funding will be made unanswerable.

‘We need facts or what is called data,’ said Ogilvie. ‘We are trying to do some studies with universities to get that data — physical and mental — and get it to the government. We want to prove the benefits and then we could make this prescriptive through surgeries.

‘We see the benefits day to day anecdotally but that doesn’t bring you the data. Sponsorship helps.

Walking Football attracts thousands of participants at clubs across the country

‘The university studies won’t come overnight because they need to be detailed. But if we could get to the stage where we could prove the benefits, then the NHS and the government would see that proof in black and white.’

This is all serious and proper. But both men were keen to emphasise that the game was fun. Ogilvie said: ‘When I started, I asked someone: “How would you sum up walking football?” He said to me: “It’s a cross between watching Barcelona and the Gurkha warriors”.’

He added: ‘I loved when at the end of an over-75s tournament one player said to another: “Good game, son”.’

The football world has thus moved into a new era. But some things cannot change. Ogilvie said: ‘One of my grandsons, who is 10, came along to watch a session and said two things. Firstly, it is a bit more intense than he thought and second there are no pink boots.’

Riley chimed in: ‘That would be an affront, that would be unacceptable.’

Even in walking football some things are a step too far.

■ Eric Riley and Campbell Ogilvie were speaking at the announcement of William Hill as official sponsor of Walking Football Scotland. To find your nearest game visit walkingfootballscotland.org

#1305. 10 Tallest Players in the Premier League Right Now (Ranked)

Having done law at LSE, Vijievan transitioned into the world of sports journalism through a fast-track diploma course with the Press Association. After completing that, he did an internship at 90min, before joining the Snack Media team on a full-time basis.

Initially starting off as a writer for FootballFanCast, Vijievan became assistant editor of the site and weekend editor of This is Futbol. After a few years working across both sites, he took up the role of assistant editor to the exclusives project at GiveMeSport, speaking to a number of top journalists like Fabrizio Romano and Christian Falk on the latest transfer news across European football.

Now taking on the role of evergreen editor, Vijievan is responsible for longer-form content based on everything from the Premier League to international football. Outside of that, he's also passionate about cricket and the NBA.

The Premier League has been host to plenty of footballing giants in the past, with the legendary figure Peter Crouch particularly standing out. But who are the tallest in the Premier League right now? While footballers come in all different shapes and sizes, having a tall frame can be crucial in certain positions. Goalkeepers need to be large to fill the sticks, while defenders want to be aerially dominant against strikers and vice versa.

Those are the two positions which dominate this list of the tallest Premier League players, with both veterans and newcomers present. Newcastle United stand out, with four players in the top 10, three of them goalkeepers. So without further ado, here are the 10 tallest players in the Premier League right now.

Everton defender Jake O’Brien is among the tallest Premier League players at 197cm. The versatile ace joined the club from Lyon and was a regular in the Toffees' lineup in 2025/26, though he has had to fight for minutes since. The Republic of Ireland international is a player with plenty of potential, having been a regular for French side Lyon before his move to Goodison. He is dangerous in both boxes, providing a goal threat, and his ability to play across the back-line makes him such an invaluable member of David Moyes's squad.

One of three towering goalkeepers at St James' Park, Lukas Hornicek arrived from Braga in the 2026 summer transfer window after Newcastle met his €30million release clause. The Czech Republic international made 88 appearances for the Portuguese side, keeping 37 clean sheets, and helped them to the Europa League semi-finals in 2025/26. Signed to be first choice, Hornicek has taken the gloves from long-serving No.1 Nick Pope under head coach Matthias Jaissle.

A giant central defender, Jair Cunha joined Nottingham Forest from Botafogo in 2025 and made his debut in the Carabao Cup against Swansea. Injuries, including a foot problem, disrupted his first season in England, but the Brazilian still made nine Premier League appearances and featured in Forest's Europa League campaign. While Cunha's height makes him invaluable when defending and attacking set-pieces, the 21-year-old has been handed more first-team opportunities in 2026/27, netting in the win over Manchester City.

Another goalkeeper to make the list, Newcastle's Pope stands at 198cm. Injuries have curtailed some of his progress in recent seasons, but when fit, however, Pope is one of the most reliable goalkeepers in the league. He was part of the squad that won the 2025 Carabao Cup, but the summer arrivals of Hornicek and Ewen Jaouen have pushed him down the pecking order. Before his move to Newcastle in 2022, he spent six years at Burnley, where he was named in the 2019/20 PFA Team of the Year.

Brentford's sole representative on the list, Kristoffer Ajer was an absolute star at Celtic, developing into a genuine ball-playing centre-back who could carry the ball up the pitch. So his move to the Bees after a few years at Parkhead was seen as a significant coup. While he perhaps hasn't developed into the dominant, modern-day centre-half that many seemed to tip him to be early on in his career, he passed 100 Premier League appearances in 2025/26 and has committed his future to the club until 2030.

Newcastle's first signing of the 2026 summer transfer window, Ewen Jaouen arrived from Reims for a reported £18.5million. The France Under-21 international kept a division-high 15 clean sheets in Ligue 2 in 2025/26, having previously starred on loan at Dunkerque during their run to the Coupe de France semi-finals. Standing at two metres tall, the 20-year-old is viewed as a long-term option between the sticks at St James' Park.

Chelsea agreed a deal to sign Mike Penders from Genk in 2024, with the Belgian goalkeeper joining the club in the summer of 2025. He was immediately loaned to Strasbourg, where he made 33 Ligue 1 appearances, before returning to Stamford Bridge for 2026/27.

With Robert Sanchez leaving for Como on loan, the 21-year-old provides competition for Emiliano Martínez, and his contract runs until 2032.

After seven years at Leeds United, Illan Meslier joined Premier League champions Arsenal on a free transfer in the summer of 2026. The Frenchman perhaps hasn't progressed as was initially expected from him, and he lost his place at Elland Road following the arrival of Lucas Perri, failing to make a competitive appearance in 2025/26. A favourite of Marcelo Bielsa during Leeds' last spell in the top flight, Meslier now provides back-up to David Raya at the Emirates.

At a giant 201cm, Newcastle defender Dan Burn is the tallest outfield player in the Premier League right now. Naturally, his height makes him a very strong and aerially dominant centre-back, but he provides a versatility which allows managers to put him on the left side of a back three, or even as a wing-back. He has been at the club since 2022, joining from Brighton. Burn has played a huge role in Newcastle's success, helping them to a Champions League berth in 2023 and again in 2025, and scoring the opener in the 2025 Carabao Cup final win over Liverpool. The England international was named club captain ahead of the 2026/27 campaign.

At 206cm, Ipswich Town goalkeeper Kjell Scherpen is the tallest player in the Premier League right now, and the tallest ever to play in the competition. The Dutchman broke Costel Pantilimon's record on his Premier League debut against Sunderland on the opening weekend of 2026/27, having never made a top-flight appearance during his earlier spell at Brighton.

Ipswich signed Scherpen from Union Saint-Gilloise on a four-year deal, and while he has faced competition from Christian Walton for the No.1 shirt, his reach makes him a commanding presence in the box.

#1304. Trafford shows he has credentials to dislodge Pickford as England No 1

Has there been a better goalkeeper in the Premier League this season than Leeds United’s James Trafford? It is a question worth asking after his brilliance secured his side a point against Sunderland.

Opinions will vary, of course, but the body of evidence to back Trafford’s argument to permanently dislodge Jordan Pickford as England No 1 looked even stronger at the Stadium of Light.

After leaving Manchester City in the summer to play regularly following a frustrating season as backup, Trafford is proving to be a brilliant buy for Leeds. He is the most expensive British goalkeeper. More importantly, he is playing like it too.

This was a tough examination for Leeds, who were not at their best, against a typically robust and physically challenging Sunderland who are getting back to doing the things that made them so difficult to play against last season. Regis Le Bris’ side created the better chances but were repeatedly denied by Trafford.

With the windy weather playing havoc, ruining the game as a spectacle, as both sides struggled for control of the ball, the two moments of quality came from Trafford in the first half.

Goalkeeping is defined by athleticism, physical strength and reflexes, but it is also about decision-making and mental fortitude. The two saves Trafford made to deny Sunderland’s Brian Brobbey in the first half were very different, but equally impressive.

The first was deceptively hard. Although the connection on Brobbey’s shot – back in the Sunderland side and causing chaos as usual – from the edge of the area was not the cleanest and that almost made it harder, as the flight of the ball was difficult to pick up. The bounce just in front of the goalkeeper meant he had to watch it closely, judge the trajectory in the air and spin off the grass and still keep a strong hand, at full stretch, to push it away from danger.

The second was, arguably, even better. Trafford had come off his line as Brobbey ran into the box. He was in a really vulnerable position, well outside his six-yard box in a one-on-one with the Netherlands international. The way he kept calm, stood up and timed when to move for the ball was superb, especially as an error could have led to a penalty.

Trafford may have saved with his feet, but he had cramped Brobbey for room, waited for the centre forward to make a move and timed the moment to dive at his feet perfectly. It was elite-level goalkeeping in a really tricky situation that favoured the striker.

Trafford made two more fine stops in the second half too, both from Nilson Angulo. The first was getting down low to tip another bouncing ball wide, which had flicked off a defender too. The second punching another deflected effort away after a block had taken some of the venom out of the shot.

Sunderland will feel like they shaded the battle, but Robin Roefs also made two decent stops from long-range shots in the second half while substitute Sean Longstaff saw an injury-time effort cleared off the line.

“It’s a positive [point],” said Le Bris. “The more positive [thing] is the way we played with intensity, togetherness - we were Sunderland today.”
